stories.label: 中国异构计算何以“顶天立地”？
stories.summary: A Chinese-built 100,000-accelerator AI supercluster, Sugon's Shuguang 8000 in Zhengzhou, powered this year's ACM Gordon Bell Prize winner at SC26: an AI wavefunction calculation of nitrogenase's iron-molybdenum cofactor (113 electrons, 76 orbitals), with a 1.5km global weather model also a climate-prize finalist. Lead with the sanctions angle: all-domestic hardware, under US export controls, taking HPC's top application prize, scaling to 45,000 cards at 94.9% efficiency. The source is an industry-friendly mainland outlet; attribute the performance figures to it.

stories.label: 跨境收款之后，中国公司盯上智能体支付的新生意
stories.summary: Chinese cross-border payment firms are moving into 'agent payments', where AI agents pay on a business's behalf. The model shifts from charging channel fees to embedding operations inside companies' daily workflows. Lead with the mechanism: who holds the money and the liability when software, not a person, authorises a payment, and how Chinese firms are trying to set that standard before Western card networks do.

stories.label: 大众花巨资买软件，想拿回什么？
stories.summary: After three straight years of losses at its software unit CARIAD, Volkswagen has changed how it develops software and is buying it in at great expense, including from Chinese partners. Lead with the reversal: Europe's biggest carmaker is paying to import the software stack it failed to build, and China's EV makers now set the pace in the car's most valuable layer.

stories.label: Indonesia factory fire kills three, 36 missing
stories.summary: A fire destroyed the three-storey Fonusa Agung Mulia sweets factory in Serang, Banten, near Jakarta. At least three workers are dead and 36 missing; SCMP reports seven body bags recovered and up to 50 sought. Lead with the workers and the toll, then the accountability question: exits, fire licensing and inspection at Banten's dense industrial belt, and who answers for it.

stories.label: 'Population up in 40 China-border villages': Amit Shah reaches out to Arunachal amid dam protests
stories.summary: Delhi is courting Arunachal Pradesh while indigenous communities protest a mega-dam on the Siang. Amit Shah cites population growth in 40 China-border villages, and Kiren Rijiju calls for a 'balance' between tribal rights and investment. Lead with who bears the cost: Adi villages facing submergence for a dam Delhi frames as a strategic answer to China's Yarlung Tsangpo project upstream, so national security is being used to override land rights.

stories.label: Opposition questions US policy after report flags China's support to Pakistan during Op Sindoor
stories.summary: The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission's annual report says Chinese military support for Pakistan during the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict complicated India's operations, and India's opposition is now questioning Washington's policy. Lead with what the commission documents about China's role (an independent US body, not government policy) and why it matters: the first major conflict where Chinese weapons and support were tested against a Western-armed military. Give Pakistan's position too; no Pakistani outlet is in the feed.

stories.label: Ukraine delivers massive strike on DPR's energy infrastructure overnight
stories.summary: State media only: Russian state news agency TASS reports that an overnight Ukrainian strike on energy facilities cut power to a large part of Russian-occupied Donetsk, quoting the occupation 'prime minister' Andrey Chertkov. Attribute every claim to TASS and the Russian-installed authorities. Frame it as the mirror image of Russia's long campaign against Ukraine's grid: civilians on both sides of the line now go into winter without power.

stories.label: Investors drive gold market as prices fall in Karachi
stories.summary: Gold's worst week in years has turned into a buying rush in Karachi. Heavy investor demand has emptied dealers of gold bars, which now carry premiums of Rs10,000-30,000 per tola, while wedding shoppers come back from silver and imitation jewellery. Lead with the bar shortage: Pakistanis treat gold as the savings account they trust over the rupee and the banks. Name the series: the gold price.

stories.label: Hormuz standoff puts Jordan in investment spotlight but transformation remains gradual | The National
stories.summary: The economic war in the Strait of Hormuz has pushed European governments to look for trade and energy routes that avoid the Gulf, and Jordan is being courted as a land bridge and electricity partner. Lead with the mechanism: a war 1,000km away is redrawing which Arab states Europe invests in. Then the catch: an IMF programme, debt and slow reform mean the change in Jordan is gradual. Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: UK maritime agency reports second attack today on tanker in Hormuz
stories.summary: New development: two separate tanker attacks in one day off Oman's Khasab, on the outbound lane of the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran saying one vessel struck a naval mine. A mine is a different threat from a missile: it stays in the water after a ceasefire and keeps insurers out. The same day Foreign Minister Araghchi said reopening the strait is 'irrelevant' until Iran's demands are met. Tie it to ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude, and to who pays: Gulf exporters and the Asian importers behind them.

stories.label: Italy's ex-police chief dies amid probe into mafia case cover-up; suicide suspected
stories.summary: Gianni De Gennaro, Italy's national police chief and later intelligence coordinator, was under investigation for obstructing a reopened probe into the 1992 murder of anti-mafia magistrate Paolo Borsellino when he apparently took his own life at 78. Lead with the accountability question: 34 years on, the state's own top officers are suspects in hiding who killed the judge, and the death may close a line of inquiry. Report the death with care, without method detail.

stories.label: Denmark calls for restrictions for Russians after alleged rapper assassination plot
stories.summary: New development after the 2026-11-20 expulsion: Denmark has sent EU members a note asking them to issue Russians limited-territory visas that do not allow travel across Schengen, citing the foiled plot to kill Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner. Lead with the mechanism: one state's security case is being turned into a bloc-wide visa rule, and the cost falls on ordinary Russian travellers as well as agents.

stories.label: 'Horrific' arrests at Seattle airport fuels anger at 'beyond reform' ICE
stories.summary: Masked ICE agents pulled travellers off a crowded jet bridge at Seattle-Tacoma, wrestling at least one woman to the ground and delaying a Los Angeles flight, and Washington's governor and a union have denounced it. Lead with the new ground: enforcement has moved past the security line onto the boarding bridge, during Thanksgiving travel. Name who was detained if the sources do, and what the state can and cannot do to stop federal agents in its airport. Use Reuters for facts over the Post's framing.

stories.label: Azerbaijan president begins 3-day visit to Vietnam
stories.summary: Ilham Aliyev and Vietnam's Prime Minister Le Minh Hung agreed in Hanoi to widen oil and gas, investment and trade ties, and to link rail freight through the Trans-Caspian (Middle) Corridor. Lead with the why: with Hormuz shut, Caspian producers and Asian buyers are looking for routes and suppliers that avoid the Gulf. Name what was actually signed, not the courtesy language.

stories.label: On defence, Japan's Takaichi caught between a weak yen and Trump
stories.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi plans to rein in Japan's next five-year defence budget because a weak yen makes imported US weapons dearer and tax cuts have narrowed the fiscal room, and conservatives in her own party are pushing back while Washington wants more. Lead with the mechanism: the yen's fall is a defence-policy constraint, since much of the budget buys American hardware priced in dollars. Name the yen as the series.

stories.label: Pentagon moves to restrict defence ties with Canada
stories.summary: Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has issued a classified memo restricting military cooperation with Canada, a NATO ally and NORAD partner, and the Pentagon says it is 'refocusing' the relationship on American priorities. Lead with what is actually restricted, and with the structural point: the US is applying pressure to its closest ally through defence ties that both countries' continental air defence depends on. Dateline Ottawa if the effect lands there.

stories.label: South Korea education minister Choi Kyo-jin resigns amid AI cheating scandal
stories.summary: South Korea's education minister resigned on Sunday after an AI-assisted cheating scandal that began when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam was found to have used AI, and spread to fears over the college entrance exam (suneung) last week. Lead with the precedent: the first cabinet minister to fall over AI cheating, in the country whose whole education system rests on one high-stakes exam. Explain how the cheating worked and what exam security is changing.

stories.label: 小鹏交出一份增长财报，盈利拐点为何还没来？
stories.summary: Xpeng posted record third-quarter revenue and deliveries yet still is not profitable. TMTPost asks why the profit turning point has not arrived, and whether overseas expansion and 'physical AI' (robotaxis, humanoid robots) can carry it. Lead with the gap between volume and margin in China's EV price war, from the mainland tech press's own reading, and give the figures.

stories.label: AI is being used to clone real people's videos
stories.summary: AI-generated characters on social media are copying real creators' videos frame by frame (their performances, their music, their scripts) and posting them as synthetic accounts that compete with the originals. Lead with a named creator whose work was cloned and with what the platforms do or fail to do when the copy is reported. The mechanism is that likeness and performance have no protection that the copiers have to respect.

stories.label: Tinubu campaigns in Ibadan, says Nigeria on path to prosperity
stories.summary: Nigeria's 2027 presidential race opened in Ibadan: Tinubu told the South-west that the sacrifices of his reforms (fuel-subsidy removal, the floated naira) will soon pay off, while Oyo governor Seyi Makinde's campaign, now a rival bid, mocked the rally's turnout and his four-year record, and the Wike-backed PDP disowned the opposition coalition and threatened to sue members who join it. Lead with the promise of prosperity against what the reforms cost households; the mechanism is an opposition split between a coalition and a PDP faction aligned with the president, which helps an incumbent. Dateline Ibadan.

stories.label: UK man swims in Strait of Hormuz to highlight environmental damage
stories.summary: The swim is the hook, not the story: Lewis Pugh, the UN Patron of the Oceans, swam in the Strait of Hormuz to document what months of attacks on oil tankers and gas carriers have spilled into one of the world's busiest waterways, and called for it to be reopened and cleaned up. Lead with the pollution nobody is counting and who lives off these waters (Omani and Iranian fishing communities); tie it to the collapse in ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz under the blockade. Do not re-report the blockade itself, covered this cycle.

stories.label: BJP Accepts Public Mandate Following Loss In Rajasthan Local Elections
stories.summary: Congress won the Zila Parishad (district council) polls in Rajasthan, a state the BJP has governed since 2023, and the BJP state president conceded. Lead with the scale of the Congress win in the rural tier and why panchayat results matter: they are the widest test of rural anti-incumbency against a ruling party between state elections. Name the numbers the source gives; do not inflate a local result into a national verdict. Dateline Jaipur.

stories.label: Social norm strength varies between cultures with respect to norm referent, norm type, contextualization, normative properties, and valence - Communications Psychology
stories.summary: A cross-cultural study tests the leading theory that societies are simply 'tight' or 'loose' about norms, and finds instead that how strongly a norm binds depends on whose expectation it is, what kind of rule it is and the context. Lead with the most striking cross-country contrast the paper reports; the point for the reader is that a single tightness score for a whole culture, Muslim-majority ones included, hides more than it shows.

stories.label: Iran will break US naval blockade: Gharibabadi
stories.summary: The new development: Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi called the US naval blockade an act of war and vowed to break it, and the same day Bahrain said an Iranian strike hit an industrial site as tankers were struck in Hormuz, while the IRGC claimed hits on the US bases at Sheikh Isa and Juffair (Mehr, state media — attribute) even as Qatari mediators held talks in Tehran. Lead with Bahrain's own statement and the tankers; the stakes are ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude. Iranian claims must be attributed as state-agency reports.

stories.label: Fossil fuel talks deadlock pushes COP31 climate summit into overtime
stories.summary: New since our presidency story: the Antalya summit has run past its deadline, deadlocked among almost 200 nations on three named fights — a fossil-fuel transition, finance flows to developing economies, and the timing of the next IPCC reports. Lead with who is blocking what, and who pays for delay: the climate-vulnerable states waiting on finance.

stories.label: Niger village attack sparks deadly reprisals
stories.summary: A dawn attack on a Kambari community in Borgu, Niger State, killed many and set off reprisals against Fulani residents, in a cycle fed by Boko Haram-linked attacks. Lead with the dead on both sides, named and counted equally, and the mechanism: armed groups turning communal grievance into ethnic war while the state is absent.

stories.label: Trump Moves to Restrict Congressional Oversight of Contractors
stories.summary: An executive order now requires federal contractors to get White House permission before answering congressional requests for information — a pre-emptive wall against the investigations Democrats plan. Lead with the mechanism: oversight of public money routed through private firms, and the contracting leverage that makes firms comply.

stories.label: Growing up displaced in Cameroon after ten years of conflict
stories.summary: Ten years into Cameroon's Anglophone war, displaced children in Buea trade in markets to feed their families while schooling lapses. A forgotten displacement is the story: lead with the scale of the displaced and the lost school years, and name the separatists and the state forces whose fighting keeps them out of home.

stories.label: At least 144 detained across France during protests against rising prices -- ministry
stories.summary: At least 144 people were detained in protests against rising prices across French cities, per interior-ministry figures relayed by BFMTV and reported by Russian state news agency TASS (attribute; no independent source in the feed). Lead with the cost-of-living grievance — energy and food prices pushed up by the Gulf war — and the policing response.

stories.label: BepiColombo finally reaches Mercury after eight-year odyssey
stories.summary: The European-Japanese BepiColombo craft entered Mercury orbit after eight years, only the second mission ever after NASA's MESSENGER. Lead with why it took eight years — braking against the Sun's gravity needs nine flybys — and the open questions its two orbiters will test: Mercury's oversized iron core and its odd magnetic field.

stories.label: Low-dose aspirin use and the risk of synchronous metastatic colorectal cancer: results from a population-based study - British Journal of Cancer
stories.summary: A population-based study in the British Journal of Cancer asks whether people taking daily low-dose aspirin are less likely to already have distant metastases when colorectal cancer is diagnosed. Lead with the effect size and dose-response, and be plain that this is observational: it shows association, not that aspirin prevents spread.

stories.label: Tesla's Assisted Driving System Gets The Green Light For Rollout In Italy
stories.summary: Italy's transport ministry under Matteo Salvini gave provisional approval to Tesla's supervised self-driving, rebranded 'Assisted Driving' in Europe, after the Dutch type-approval. Lead with the regulatory mechanism: one EU state's approval opens a path across the bloc, and national ministers are now deciding what EU-wide safety rules have not.

stories.label: Repeated bending strengthens sugar-based hydrogel instead of wearing it down
stories.summary: Chenfeng Ke's team at Washington University in St. Louis made a sugar-based polymer that gets stronger the more it is bent, the reverse of ordinary fatigue. Lead with the measured gain in strength per cycle and the mechanism that makes stress rebuild the network, then the uses: soft robotics, implants, wearables.

stories.label: Vance stops short of endorsing Trump's claim that Iran was close to nuclear weapon
stories.summary: Two signals on the same question in one day: in Washington, Vice-President Vance declined to back Trump's claim that Iran was weeks from a bomb in February — the claim the war was sold on — while in Tehran Foreign Minister Araghchi said there is a 'major strategic debate' over Iran's nuclear doctrine and that the enriched-uranium stockpile will be used according to needs 'however they are defined'. Lead with Araghchi's words: the war meant to stop a weapon is pushing Tehran to say aloud that it may want one. Dateline Tehran; attribute Trump's claim as unverified.

stories.label: EU Proposes New Cuts to Long-Term Budget to Bridge Policy Divide
stories.summary: European Council president António Costa has cut back the bloc's next seven-year budget and proposed an EU-wide tax on digital services to pay for it. Lead with the digital tax: a levy that lands mostly on US tech platforms, proposed while Washington threatens tariffs over exactly such taxes. Explain the divide being bridged — net payers wanting less, farm and cohesion states wanting their shares — and that even the cut plan is about a quarter above current spending. Name the euro as the series. Dateline Brussels.

stories.label: Has AI's honeymoon ended on Wall Street?
stories.summary: New since our chip-crash story: the week's toll. The Nasdaq fell 5.28% as investors balked at AI capital spending with no profit in sight; Micron lost 23.6% in the week, TSMC 14.9% and ASML 12.8%, and bitcoin hit $55,130, its lowest since September 2024, before bouncing back above $60,000 (CoinDesk). Lead with the chipmakers, the firms that sold the picks and shovels, and the mechanism: markets pricing a Fed hike while doubting the payback on data centres. Name bitcoin and the US 10-year Treasury yield as the series. Dateline New York.

stories.label: US denies Iran hit F-16 fighter jet
stories.summary: Iran says its air defences hit a US F-16 over the Strait of Hormuz and the IRGC says it downed another US reconnaissance drone off Bushehr, after what state broadcaster IRIB called one of its most intense operations against 'trespassing' vessels overnight; CENTCOM says no F-16 was attacked 'at all'. Lead with the two irreconcilable accounts, attributing each, then what is not disputed: a Qatari delegation is in Tehran for talks on ending the war (The New Arab) while the US blockade holds. Name ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude as the series. Iranian claims come from state media (Mehr, IRIB via TASS): say so. Dateline Bandar Abbas.

stories.label: India's opposition stages protests against Meta over account removals
stories.summary: Congress's youth wing protested outside Meta offices in three cities and gave the company a seven-day ultimatum to restore removed and restricted opposition accounts. Lead with who decides what India's opposition can say online: a US platform acting, by the opposition's account, on government takedown demands. Explain the mechanism — India's IT Rules blocking orders and how platforms comply — and how many accounts were affected. Dateline Hyderabad.

stories.label: Saudi-led coalition intercepts three Houthi missiles headed for Riyadh
stories.summary: New since our 20 November story on the Houthis' claimed strike on a Saudi power plant and port: the coalition says it intercepted three ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, and the capital got emergency alerts for a third night running. Lead with Riyadh under nightly alert — the Saudi-Houthi truce that held since 2022 is effectively over. Explain the tit-for-tat on power infrastructure (Saada, Mokha, Hodeidah) and who pays: Yemeni civilians already without electricity. Dateline Riyadh.

stories.label: Manipur Hooch Tragedy: Death Toll Rises To 21, Nearly 600 Hospitalised After Consuming 'Spurious' Liquor
stories.summary: Twenty-one dead and about 600 in hospital after drinking contaminated liquor in Manipur's Chandel district. Lead with the scale — 600 poisoned points to a supply chain, not one bad batch — and ask who sold it and who let it be sold: Manipur's partial prohibition pushes drinking into an unregulated market, and methanol is the usual killer. Name what the state government has done (arrests, compensation). Dateline Chandel.

stories.label: Flood displaces families in upscale Akwa Ibom estate
stories.summary: Weeks of flooding have driven families from an estate in Uyo, and Premium Times asks where the billions of naira budgeted for flood control and emergency response went. Lead with the budget against the water: what Akwa Ibom allocated, what was built, and who approved building on a floodplain. This is an accountability story about drainage and building approvals, not weather. Name the naira as the series only if the report gives sums. Dateline Uyo.

stories.label: Image-guided versus local field potential-guided programming for subthalamic deep brain stimulation in Parkinson's disease - npj Parkinson's Disease
stories.summary: A crossover study compares two ways of tuning the brain implants used for Parkinson's: guided by imaging of where the electrode sits, or by the brain's own electrical signals (local field potentials). Lead with which method controlled symptoms better and how much clinician time it saved — programming a stimulator can take months of clinic visits, which is why most patients in poorer countries never get it. Keep to what the trial found and its size.

stories.label: Race realism" isn't realistic -- and it isn't good science
stories.summary: After Trump called Somalis 'low-IQ people' at Davos, Ars sets out what modern genetics actually shows: human genetic variation does not sort into races, most of it lies within populations, and polygenic scores for educational attainment collapse outside the populations they were trained on. Lead with the evidence, not the rhetoric — the reader wants the science that answers a head of state's claim about a Muslim nation. Report the findings cited, not the author's opinion.

stories.label: 并表和IP，不是腾讯音乐的长效药
stories.summary: TMTPost, from inside China's tech press, argues Tencent Music's latest results are propped up by consolidating acquisitions and selling IP merchandise rather than growth in paid streaming — it is turning into a consumer-goods company. Lead with the figures behind that: subscriber growth against revenue from consolidated units and merchandise. The mechanism: China's music-streaming market has saturated, and the leader is buying growth.

stories.label: Finnish border guards head towards drone-hit cargo ship
stories.summary: A cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad was hit by two drones in the Gulf of Finland, three nautical miles from Russia's border, and is now burning in Finnish waters with its crew being evacuated. Lead with where it happened: the war at sea has reached the Baltic route that keeps Russia's exclave supplied, beside a NATO member's coast. Attribute Russian officials' account and the Kaliningrad governor's 'no threat to supplies' line to TASS; Finland's border guard is the independent voice. Nobody has claimed it — say so. Dateline Gulf of Finland / Helsinki.

stories.label: Russian missiles hit Poland: What happened, and could NATO respond?
stories.summary: Follow-up to our 11-20 story on the suspected missile in Lublin province. The new development: Warsaw now says it may have been hit by two missiles, security cameras caught the impact, and the government calls it an intentional Russian provocation, not stray debris. Lead with that shift from 'investigating' to an accusation. Then explain the mechanism: what Article 4 consultations and Article 5 each require, and why the bar for collective defence stays high. Dateline Warsaw.

stories.label: Ballistic missile attack on Zelenskyy's hometown kills two people
stories.summary: A Russian ballistic missile on Kryvyi Rih killed a seven-year-old boy and a young paramedic. Lead with the two dead by name if the sources give them, and with the paramedic: a responder killed in a city that has been hit again and again. The mechanism: ballistic missiles give minutes or none of warning, so air defence and shelters fail first in cities near the front. Note Zelensky calling Putin a 'killer' while Washington courts Moscow over a January deal deadline. Dateline Kryvyi Rih.

stories.label: COP31: Nigerian, global groups accuse presidencies of risking 'disappointing' climate deal
stories.summary: As COP31 in Antalya runs into its final hours, a coalition of 100 civil society groups led from Nigeria says the joint Türkiye–Australia presidency failed to steer the talks, letting climate finance, adaptation and the fossil-fuel transition weaken. Lead with who is speaking: Global South groups whose countries carry the cost of warming they did not cause. The mechanism: a split presidency with no single broker. This follows our stories on the draft dropping fossil-fuel language and on net-negative emissions. Dateline Antalya.

stories.label: Overturned boat carrying mourners to funeral kills at least four in Nigeria
stories.summary: A boat believed to carry hundreds of mourners to a funeral capsized in Bayelsa State after a mechanical failure; at least four are dead, two of them children, and the search goes on. Lead with the gap between hundreds aboard and four counted. The mechanism: in the creeks of the Niger Delta boats are the only road, and overloading and missing life jackets go unenforced, so capsizes recur every year. Dateline Bayelsa State.

stories.label: Minister clashes with BBC host on UK-EU tuition fees talks - 'you're the expert'
stories.summary: Report the substance, not the radio row: Friday's UK-EU summit agreed deals that ministers insist are not at risk, while a dispute over what EU students pay at British universities hangs over them. Lead with what was agreed at the summit and what Brussels wants on tuition fees in return. The mechanism: the EU ties market access to youth mobility and fee parity, so a university-funding question becomes a trade lever. Who pays: UK universities that rely on higher international fees. Dateline London.

stories.label: ETH news: Ether's plunge puts a Nasdaq-listed treasury in a $54 million loan squeeze
stories.summary: BTCS, a Nasdaq-listed company whose main asset is ether, told the SEC it cannot rule out liquidation of a $54 million Aave loan backed by that ether, even after paying down about $10 million in ten days. Lead with the filing. The mechanism: 'crypto treasury' firms borrowed against the coin they hold, so a falling price shrinks the collateral and can force a sale that pushes the price lower. Context: bitcoin at a two-year low after the Fed's hikes. Dateline New York.

stories.label: Signal Cracks Down on AI Agents, Says They Threaten Users' Privacy
stories.summary: Signal is blocking OS-level AI agents such as Google's Gemini and Apple's Siri from screen-capturing its chats. Lead with the threat model: end-to-end encryption protects a message in transit, but an assistant that reads the screen takes it after decryption, at the operating-system layer the app does not control. Who is exposed: the journalists, officials and dissidents who rely on Signal. Explain what Signal can block and what it cannot.

stories.label: Denmark's GomSpace Secures €8M Contract for Blue Origin Moon Mission
stories.summary: Danish satellite maker GomSpace won an €8 million phase-two contract to build two spacecraft for a lunar resource-prospecting mission. Its announcement names only a 'leading North American' customer; European Spaceflight identifies it as Blue Origin. Lead with the hidden customer and what the craft are meant to prospect for. The structural point: European small-satellite firms are becoming suppliers to a US-led race to claim resources on the Moon. Dateline Aalborg.

stories.label: An ancient failed rift is reawakening inside one of Africa's oldest landmasses
stories.summary: The magnitude 6.5 earthquake of April 2017 in eastern Botswana came from the middle of the Kalahari Craton, crust up to 3.7 billion years old that geologists thought too cold and thick to tear. New work finds an ancient failed rift there reactivating. Lead with that 2017 quake and why it should not have happened. The mechanism: what is weakening the old rift. Why it matters: seismic hazard in a region whose buildings were never designed for it. Dateline Gaborone.

stories.label: Scientists Discover New and Horrible Eagle-Based Way Our Ancestors Died
stories.summary: Researchers documented eagles in Chad hunting large adult baboons, prey far heavier than thought possible. That suggests birds of prey threatened early humans and other hominins later in our evolution than believed. Lead with the observed kill and the animal's size. The mechanism: what talon marks on fossil skulls, like the Taung child's, now mean when read against live behaviour. Dateline Chad.
